text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
- Opposition party FIDESZ said it will initiate a referendum if the cabinet submits to Parliament its proposals for amending the land law.
- Deputy Speaker of Parliament Tibor Fuzessy announced Friday that Parliament will begin detailed debate on the planned pension scheme on Monday.
- The Socialists and the Young Democrats top a recent Gallup poll with 30% support and 27%, respectively, among decided voters.
- The Socialist Party will field its own candidates at next year's elections, national council chairman Ferenc Baja told a Saturday press briefing.
- Istvan Csurka, president of the far-right Hungarian Justice and Life Party (MIEP) warned Friday that if nationalist forces take power, they will review what he called thieves' privatization.
- Farmers protests planned for Friday apparently drew little support and caused minimal disruption.
- Prime Minister Gyula Horn held several one-to-one meetings after Friday's gathering of EU leaders and the heads of government of associate members in Amsterdam.
- The crawling peg inflation rate can only be decreased if the wage agreement between the government and employees is adhered to, National Bank board member Tibor Erdos warns.
- A bipartisan delegation of the US Senate is to visit to Hungary and subsequently Poland in connection with an impending official announcement on NATO expansion.
- Gabor Szeles, president and CEO of the bus maker Ikarus Rt., will set up a consortium to bid for the state-owned company when it is privatized later this year.
- Hungary's foreign trade mission network will be phased out as of tomorrow, July 1.

- The government is deliberately underestimating this year's inflation and the trade deficit is going to be higher than expected, according to the latest, modified prognosis of the Privatization Research Institute.
- The Hungarian Telephone & Cable Corp. (HTCC) plans to participate in the privatization of the broadcasting company Antenna Hungaria.
